summary: INQHIST is an online CICS program that handles a Transaction History Inquiry. It first connects to DB2 through a helper program (DB2ONLN); if the connect fails it invokes a recovery helper (DB2RECV) and retries. It then builds a SQL SELECT of the last transactions for the account (from the POSHIST table, newest first) and runs it through a cursor manager helper (CURSMGR) using a declare -> open -> fetch -> close sequence, loading up to 10 history rows into a working table. Finally it sends the formatted history to the user's screen via CICS map HISMAP (mapset INQSET). Errors route to an error routine that returns the SQLCODE to the caller. Error conditions handled: DB2 connect failure (with recovery + retry) and general CICS errors.

paragraphs.name: MAINLINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
-- Program driver
CALL P100-INIT-PROGRAM      -- set up + connect to DB2
CALL P200-GET-HISTORY       -- run the cursor and fetch rows
CALL P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY    -- show history on screen
CICS RETURN TO caller
paragraphs.notes: Unnamed mainline is the true entry driver.

paragraphs.name: P100-INIT-PROGRAM
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET WS-COMMAREA = DFHCOMMAREA   -- copy caller's comm-area in
CLEAR WS-ROW-COUNT              -- MOVE ZEROS
SET NO-MORE-ROWS = true
CICS HANDLE CONDITION: on ERROR -> jump to P999-ERROR-ROUTINE
CALL P150-DB2-CONNECT

paragraphs.name: P150-DB2-CONNECT
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET DB2-REQUEST-TYPE = 'C'   -- 'C' = connect
CICS LINK PROGRAM DB2ONLN  PASSING: WS-DB2-REQUEST
IF DB2-RESPONSE-CODE <> 0 THEN            -- connect failed
  SET RECV-REQUEST-TYPE = 'C'
  SET RECV-PROGRAM = 'INQHIST'
  SET RECV-SQLCODE = DB2-SQLCODE
  CICS LINK PROGRAM DB2RECV  PASSING: WS-RECOVERY-REQUEST   -- attempt recovery
  IF RECV-SUCCESS THEN
    CALL P150-DB2-CONNECT      -- retry the connect (recursion)
  ELSE
    SET inqcom_error_msg = RECV-MESSAGE
    CALL P999-ERROR-ROUTINE
  END IF
END IF
SET WS-DB2-TOKEN = DB2-CONNECTION-TOKEN
branches: IF RECV-SUCCESS -> retry connect else -> error

annotations.note: Recursive self-PERFORM on recovery success — a retry with no visible attempt limit; risk of unbounded retry if recovery keeps 'succeeding' but connect keeps failing (POTENTIAL_INFINITE_LOOP).
WS-DB2-TOKEN is not declared anywhere in this program's WORKING-STORAGE — likely defined in a copybook or is a defect; flagged for SME review.

paragraphs.notes: Connect-with-recovery-and-retry. Marked ambiguous due to the undeclared WS-DB2-TOKEN target.

paragraphs.name: P200-GET-HISTORY
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET CURS-STMT = "SELECT trans_date, trans_type, trans_units, trans_price, trans_amount FROM POSHIST WHERE account_no = ? ORDER BY trans_date DESC"
SET CURS-REQUEST-TYPE = 'D'   -- 'D' = declare cursor
CICS LINK PROGRAM CURSMGR  PASSING: WS-CURSOR-REQUEST
IF CURS-RESPONSE-CODE = 0 THEN
  SET CURS-REQUEST-TYPE = 'O'   -- 'O' = open cursor
  CICS LINK PROGRAM CURSMGR
  IF CURS-RESPONSE-CODE = 0 THEN
    CALL P250-FETCH-HISTORY
  END IF
END IF
SET CURS-REQUEST-TYPE = 'C'     -- 'C' = close cursor
CICS LINK PROGRAM CURSMGR

annotations.note: The SQL is built as text and handed to CURSMGR (a generic cursor manager) rather than run inline via EXEC SQL — an indirection layer over DB2. The '?' is a host-variable placeholder for the account number.

paragraphs.notes: Classic declare -> open -> fetch -> close cursor lifecycle, each step delegated to CURSMGR.

paragraphs.name: P250-FETCH-HISTORY
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET CURS-REQUEST-TYPE = 'F'   -- 'F' = fetch (array fetch of up to 10 rows)
CICS LINK PROGRAM CURSMGR
IF CURS-RESPONSE-CODE >= 0 THEN
  SET WS-HISTORY-TABLE = CURS-DATA-AREA   -- copy the returned rows into the 10-row history table
END IF

annotations.note: The raw data area (CURS-DATA-AREA, 3000 bytes) is bulk-moved onto WS-HISTORY-TABLE (10 x fixed rows) — the layouts must match exactly; a mismatch would silently corrupt the display.

paragraphs.name: P300-FORMAT-DISPLAY
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CICS SEND MAP HISMAP (mapset INQSET)
  FROM: WS-HISTORY-TABLE
  ERASE the screen first
  RESPONSE CODE -> ws_response_code
-- sends the history rows to the user's screen

paragraphs.name: P999-ERROR-ROUTINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET inqcom_response_code (in WS-COMMAREA) = SQLCODE   -- return the DB2 SQLCODE to the caller
SET DFHCOMMAREA = WS-COMMAREA

annotations.note: References SQLCODE directly (the DB2 host status field from SQLCA), not WS-RESPONSE-CODE.

paragraphs.notes: Reached via the ERROR HANDLE CONDITION registered in P100.
